card.name: Kaerajaan
card.era: Origin tied to an 1889 mocking song from Laaniste/Ahja; documented as a dance by Anna Raudkats in the 1910s-1920s
card.tagline: Estonia's best-known folk dance, born from a teasing song.
card.profile: Kaerajaan (Kaera-Jaan, 'Oats-Jaan / John of Oats') is a lively couple/mixer folk dance from southeastern Estonia, linked musically and structurally to the European quadrille (Univ. of Tartu; Kapper). Its name comes from a teasing song about Jaan Matson, a blacksmith's apprentice at Ahja manor known as a ladies' man; the lyric begins 'Kaera-Jaan, Kaera-Jaan...' (Tartu 2024; Tallinn University). Typically accompanied by accordion and sung melody, it features prancing steps and partner figures and is among the most widely performed dances at Estonian celebrations and abroad; a popular stage arrangement was choreographed by Mait Agu.
card.insight: Per Tartu 2024 (European Capital of Culture), the Laaniste blacksmith Jaan had no idea he inspired Estonia's best-known folk dance, still popular 135 years later; once thought purely original, kaerajaan was later recognized as linked to the international quadrille tradition (Tartu 2024; Kapper, Folklore 54).
card.image_significance: The blacksmith's teasing couple dance. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Estonia.
